s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic sinusitis with destruction of nasal structures and granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Presenting with crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections
No hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma
Occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
Normal laboratory tests, including C-reactive protein and HIV test
Substantial septal deformity and destruction of sinus septate on CT
Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum on Chest CT
Noncaseating granulomas in sinus mucosa
Growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas in culture
Positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and second FESS

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of noncaseating granulomas and destruction of nasal structures

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive AFB PCR probe and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Rhinoscleroma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic sinusitis and destruction of nasal structures

shortlist.label: Midline destructive granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Destruction of nasal structures and granulomatous inflammation

raw.rationale: Positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and second FESS, indicating mycobacterial infection

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Normal laboratory tests, including C-reactive protein and lack of other systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Presence of AFB PCR probe positivity, which is not typical for sarcoidosis

rejected.label: Rhinoscleroma
rejected.why: Lack of specific microbiological evidence for Rhinoscleroma, such as Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis

rejected.label: Midline destructive granuloma
rejected.why: Presence of AFB PCR probe positivity, which suggests a specific infectious cause rather than a destructive granuloma of unknown etiology
